claim: UCT (UCB1 at every tree node) converges on random P-game trees in about the same leaf count as alpha-beta (order B^(D/2)), and beats plain Monte Carlo and minimax-backup MC at equal budget; the bandit selection, not the tree alone, gives the gain.
agent_test: Pick among k operator branches by counted UCB vs uniform split at equal tokens on a held-out task set.

claim: UCT guarantees are asymptotic: root failure probability falls at a polynomial rate with an unspecified constant, and Coquelin and Munos show a worst case needing exp(exp(D)) rounds before the best branch is first seen; the paper does not analyse budgets of tens of rollouts, so treat the theory as design motivation only.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs rollouts 4..64 and check whether UCB beats random pick at 16 rollouts or fewer. a12 (Coquelin-Munos) was not opened.
gap_note: Gap 8 theory: Coquelin-Munos opened (d08). Deceptive-tree lower bound exp(exp(D)) confirmed. No LLM-tree test exists.
audit_note: Sources show asymptotic polynomial-rate failure and a double-exponential worst case for UCT, but Kocsis-Szepesvari only say 'some constant C' (no huge constants are shown), and the LLM-budget implication is the researcher's inference.
claim_before_audit: UCT guarantees are asymptotic (polynomial-rate failure, huge constants; worst case reported far worse) so they say little at LLM budgets of tens of rollouts; use as design motivation only.

claim: Adding a prior that fades with visits (progressive bias) plus gradual widening (progressive unpruning) lifts MCTS in wide spaces: Mango 19x19 0% to 48.2% only with both; 9x9 33.2% to 61.7%.
agent_test: Seed the branch list with a cheap-model prior that decays after n visits; compare with flat expansion at equal tokens.

claim: Coulom backup finding: mean is better at few simulations, max at many; a mix is best early (MSE 5.29 vs 6.44 mean and 41.70 max at 128 sims; max wins at 131,072: 1.83 vs 2.84).
agent_test: Compare mean vs max vs mixed backup of branch scores at 4 and 32 rollouts.

claim: MCTS with a learned policy and value (AlphaZero) beat top alpha-beta engines while searching about 1000 times fewer positions per second (80k vs 70M); averaging over noisy value errors is the authors argument, not a tested ablation.
agent_test: Test whether fewer, better-scored branches beat many unscored ones at equal tokens.

claim: Returns from search budget saturate: MuZero Atari plateaued near 100 simulations (6 simulations already useful); rStar-Math saturated by 64 trajectories; RAP-style MCTS saturated after about 4 rollouts on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct.
agent_test: Sweep rollouts 1..64 on the agent, find the knee, set the scaffold cap there.
audit_note: Minor: rStar-Math shows 'saturation or slow improvement' at 64 trajectories only on MATH, AIME and Olympiad Bench (College Math keeps improving); the 6-simulation result is for Ms. Pacman.

claim: On long-horizon planning with an explicit state model (Blocksworld), LLM MCTS (RAP) far exceeds chain of thought (LLaMA-33B 4-step 0.86-0.88 vs 0.02; Llama-2-70B full set Easy 0.65 vs 0.08), but compute is not matched (10-20 iterations vs 1 chain).
agent_test: Matched-token comparison: search with explicit state tracking vs best-of-N chains on a planning set.

claim: On arithmetic and logic reasoning the MCTS edge over self-consistency or sampling is small or absent at equal compute: RAP GSM8K 48.8 vs SC(10) 46.8; TS-LLM says CoT-SC beats tree search on GSM8K at equal tokens; Wu et al. find MCTS below sampling at every compute budget.
agent_test: Equal-token best-of-N with checker vs tree search on a GSM8K/MATH subset.
audit_note: Minor: RAP 48.8 is the text figure while the table lists RAP(1) 48.6; the RAP vs SC(10) comparison is not compute-matched; Wu et al. MCTS test is on MATH.

claim: Compute-matched, MCTS loses to simpler schemes on MATH: Wu et al. report MCTS uses dozens of times more tokens and is dominated by REBASE (about 7x less compute than sampling plus voting at equal accuracy, Llemma-7B); Snell et al. find lookahead search underperforms beam search and best-of-N at equal generation budget.
agent_test: Include balanced expansion and best-of-N as arms; MCTS must beat them at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 1: AB-MCTS d01 shows standard MCTS no better than repeated sampling at 27 calls with GPT-4o/DeepSeek-V3.
audit_note: Minor: REBASE reached higher (not equal) accuracy with about 7x less compute; 'dozens of times more tokens' is Wu et al.'s background statement, not their own measurement.

claim: Search helps on hard problems but hurts on easy ones: beam search over-exploits an imperfect verifier on easy questions (levels 1-2) at high budget and beats best-of-N only on levels 3-4.
agent_test: Gate search on a difficulty estimate; compare gated vs always-on at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 3: Snell (quantile bins), Liu (absolute thresholds, 72B model prefers best-of-N everywhere), Chen (overthinking on easy items).
audit_note: Minor: headline 'search helps on hard problems' holds for levels 3-4 only; on level 5 no method made progress, and Liu et al. show the pattern depends on policy size; all of Snell's support is one paper.

claim: The value source decides the gain: LATS ablation drops HotPotQA EM 0.63 to 0.37 without the LM heuristic and to 0.42 with DFS; prompted LLM value on Game24 (9.2-21.0) is far below learned value (64.8); rStar authors found small-model self-rewarding unreliable.
agent_test: Replace self-rated branch score with a code-checked or independent-model score; measure delta at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: LATS appendix Table 11 labels are garbled/inconsistent with main Table 8 (which gives the quoted 0.63/0.37/0.42); the prompted-vs-learned Game24 numbers are for TS-LLM with LLaMA-SFT policy.

claim: Where an executable check exists, tree search over attempts gives big gains: LATS HumanEval 83.8 (GPT-3.5) and 92.7 (GPT-4, +1.7 over Reflexion); SWE-Search +23% relative mean on SWE-bench Lite; PG-TD only small gain (26.70 vs 25.19 sampling plus filtering).
agent_test: Tree search vs sample-and-test at equal tokens on a coding set; expect a small gain.
audit_note: Minor: PG-TD 26.70 vs 25.19 is the APPS introductory pass rate for the GPT-Neo/GPT-2 setup; SWE-Search 23% is the reported mean relative gain.

claim: LATS reported numbers are internally inconsistent in places (k=50 LATS 0.63 vs 0.61; ToT 0.55 in the reasoning table vs 0.49 in the ReAct table; baselines re-implemented), so 2-6 point margins over RAP/ToT are not firm.
agent_test: Re-run baselines at matched tokens before trusting small gaps.

claim: Best-first tree search in real web environments raises success with budget, and depth and breadth must grow together: VWA 18.9 to 26.4%, WA 15.0 to 19.2%; 200-task subset 24.5 to 32.0 (5 expansions) to 37.0 (20); depth 1 breadth 1 24.5, depth 5 breadth 5 35.5-37.0.
agent_test: Run branching search on agent tasks with a resettable environment and sweep budget.

claim: Small models with MCTS plus an independent verifier gain a lot on GSM8K (rStar LLaMA2-7B 12.51 to 63.91 with 32 rollouts) but at about 167 calls and 367k tokens per question; SC@maj128 already reaches 23.05 (LLaMA2-7B) to 88.68 (Phi3). The abstract Mistral baseline 36.46 is the SC@maj8 figure; few-shot CoT is 17.89.
agent_test: Compare rStar-like diversified operators plus independent check vs SC at about 170 calls.

claim: MCTS with trained process reward models and self-evolution lifts 7B models to o1-preview level on MATH (Qwen2.5-Math-7B 58.8 to 90.0; AIME 53.3%); step-reward MCTS beats outcome-reward best-of-N (88.2-89.4 vs 82.6) but needs 747k problems and training.
agent_test: Not testable without training.
gap_note: Gap 4: rStar-Math Table 8 confounds method and reward type; round 1 without learned reward reached MATH 75.2 vs 89.4.

claim: Process-reward tree search does not beat self-consistency at first: ReST-MCTS* iteration 1 did not surpass SC; later iterations 48.5 vs 42.5; as verifier +3-4 points over SC (GSM8K 83.9 to 87.5, MATH500 35.1 to 39.0).
agent_test: Check a value signal beats voting only after calibration.
gap_note: Gap 9: ReST-MCTS* iter2 on LLaMA-3-8B average 29.02 equals few-shot 28.99.

claim: MCTS is more reliable as a teacher and data generator than as a run-time engine: AlphaMath, MCTS-DPO (+5.9 GSM8K, +5.8 MATH, +15.8 ARC-C), TS-LLM iteration (51.9 to 56.5); AlphaMath calls MCTS inference too slow and uses step beam search.
agent_test: Store verified reasoning traces and reuse as few-shot examples; test vs none.
audit_note: Minor: the 'more reliable as teacher than run-time engine' framing is the researcher's synthesis; the quoted numbers all match.

claim: DeepSeek-R1 team gave up AlphaGo-style MCTS for training: token space exponentially larger than chess, per-node extension caps gave local optima, a fine-grained value model is very hard to train; MCTS with a value model still helped at inference.
agent_test: Treat as a caution on value-model dependence.
gap_note: Gap 5: re-read this session; qualitative only, no numbers.

claim: Repeated sampling with a verifier is a strong rival to search: coverage rises log-linearly (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% with 250 samples) but without a verifier selection plateaus.
agent_test: Best-of-N with a real check as the default arm.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In wide LLM action spaces plain UCT fails without a prior: in VirtualHome plain UCT did poorly in all conditions while the LLM as prior policy and world model in PUCT won; the same shape as progressive bias in Go.
agent_test: Proposal prior with decay vs flat expansion.

claim: Generic self-reflection gives little in open tasks: LATS WebShop reflections were often generic and agents got stuck in local minima; reflection ablation only 0.63 to 0.58.
agent_test: Compare with and without reflection at equal tokens.

claim: MCTS over whole-answer refinement with LLM self-rating looks strong in small samples (MCTSr LLaMA3-8B GSM8K 74.07 to 93.03/96.66 with 4/8 rollouts) but uses self-rating and a zero-shot CoT base and is not compute matched against SC.
agent_test: Replicate with SC at matched tokens.

claim: At equal call budgets with non-reasoning frontier models (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3) fixed-width LATS-style MCTS is about equal to repeated sampling on code (LiveCodeBench 36.7 vs 37.8 and 43.2 vs 40.7) and worse on ARC-AGI (9.0 vs 15.0 and 14.0 vs 18.6); only adaptive-branching search gives a small edge on code.
agent_test: Run equal-call repeated sampling plus a checker against a small tree on 30 hard items; require a gap above one std.

claim: With reasoning models (o4-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, R1-0528) and an executable demonstration-case score, adaptive-branching tree search solved more ARC-AGI-2 public tasks than repeated sampling at equal calls (o4-mini 23% to 27.5%; multi-model over 30%; 120 tasks, coverage not Pass@2).
agent_test: Same setup on ARC items with our own model; measure Pass@k vs calls up to 50.

claim: Few LLM-MCTS papers sweep the UCT constant: LATS ablates the exploration weight at three values on HotPotQA (w=0.5 gave 0.55 EM vs 0.63 at w=1; w=2 gave no gain), TS-LLM chose c_init from only {0.3, 3.0}, and SWE-Search uses c=1.41 with no sweep found. For fixed-width MCTS on LiveCodeBench (DeepSeek-V3) width 5 scored 0.432, width 3 0.429 and width 10 0.402, so performance is sensitive to width at least at the larger setting.
agent_test: Sweep c in {0.5, 1, 1.41, 2} and width in {3, 5, 8} on 40 items at fixed 16 rollouts.
audit_note: A universal negative contradicted by its own evidence: LATS does report a 3-value exploration-weight ablation (w=0.5, 1, 2); and 'width matters more than c' is unsupported, since the 0.432 vs 0.402 width gap (std ~0.015-0.02, w=3 gives 0.429) was never compared against any c effect.
claim_before_audit: No LLM-MCTS paper reports a sweep of the UCT constant c. Evidence is thin: LATS w=0.5 gave 0.55 EM vs 0.63 at w=1 and w=2 on HotPotQA; TS-LLM tried only c_init in {0.3, 3.0}; SWE-Search uses c=1.41. The width (children per node) matters more: standard MCTS width 5 best (0.432) vs 10 (0.402).

claim: The best search method depends on model strength and difficulty: below 7B best-of-N wins easy and beam wins hard; at 72B best-of-N wins at all difficulty levels (MATH-500). Difficulty estimation costs compute (2048 samples in Snell) and was not charged.
agent_test: Gate on a cheap 3-sample agreement check; compare to always-search at equal total tokens.

claim: Internal search inside long-CoT reasoning models makes external MCTS less necessary: R1 and QwQ spend 1,953% more tokens on trivial items and first-round answers are right in over 92% of cases; DeepSeek reported MCTS helps inference only with a pre-trained value model and gave up on it for training.
agent_test: Compare external tree on a reasoning model vs the same tokens spent as longer thinking on 30 AIME-style items.

claim: UCT worst case: on a deceptive tree the best reward needs on the order of exp(exp(D)) rounds (Coquelin and Munos 2007). No LLM reasoning-tree study tests whether this happens; mitigation proposals are modified UCT, flat UCB on leaves, restarts, depth caps.
agent_test: Seed a misleading early value (a plausible wrong step scored high) and measure how many rollouts a depth-capped vs uncapped tree needs to recover.

claim: Cost overhead of agent MCTS is about 5x API cost for four models and 14x for GPT-4o in SWE-Search (23% relative gain); LATS reports tokens only on successful runs, so costs are not comparable across papers.
agent_test: Log tokens on all runs including failures and report accuracy per 100k tokens.

claim: Gain from training on MCTS traces is small: ReST-MCTS* iteration 2 on LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct averages 29.02 vs 28.99 few-shot (MATH, GPQA, CEval-Hard); no study tests storing verified traces as memory without training.
agent_test: Retrieve 3 verified traces per task type as few-shot context and compare to no memory at equal tokens.
